title: Free City of Bremen
capsule: The Free City of Bremen was a sovereign Hanseatic city-state reconstituted after the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806, when Napoleon's reorganization of Germany left Bremen in a precarious intermediate status before it was briefly annexed by the First French Empire in 1811. The Congress of Vienna (1815) restored its independence as one of the 39 sovereign members of the German Confederation, and the city-state subsequently expanded its commercial reach by purchasing from Hanover the mouth of the Weser River, where it founded Bremerhaven in 1827 as a deep-water emigrant port. Bremen's senate governed a republican polity whose prosperity rested on transatlantic trade and cotton import. In 1867 Bremen joined the North German Confederation and entered the German Empire in 1871, retaining its distinct status as a constituent free city.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The city-state's territory was small and precisely defined by its municipal limits and surrounding Hanoverian/Prussian territory; boundaries are well-documented.
